verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. The three lines are definitional in the paper; the content the paper attaches to them ("substitution into (4.16) and (4.11) gives the same formulas with X replaced by x") is what the Lean states. (a) m̂ as the five-tuple is `NominalProfile.moments`, whose value type `Debt = Fin 5 → ℝ` is the tuple (M,I,J,S,C_p). (b) The invariance (Q̂_s,N̂_s)(x,η) = (Q_s,N_s)(ρx,η) is `Qs_dilation` and `Ns_dilation`: they say the entrance-radius factors ρ^{3/2} on the angular stock and ρ on the axial stock cancel against physicalX = ρ·X and physicalH = √(2ρ)·H, leaving the unscaled Qs, Ns — i.e. Q_s and N_s do not change under the dilation, which is the paper's equation. (c) p̂_s = ρ^{-1}p_s(ρx,η) is `p1_dilation` and `p2_dilation`, in the form p_i at entrance radius XR equals XR times p_i at entrance radius 1 (the hatted value), for both components p_{s,1}, p_{s,2}. Difference in generality: (b) and (c) are stated for the constructed outgoing family (`w : ResetWitness d K`, amplitude `Amp`) and in log radial coordinates (X p = exp p.1), whereas the paper writes them for arbitrary profiles; the five-moment law of (4.19) is general (`moments_dilate`). The paper's p_s carries the factor 1/L = 1/(1−2hη²), which is also how `p1`/`p2` are defined, so the two p_s conventions agree.
